data_types.description: A string meant to represent a boolean value in textual form. Typical accepted true forms include: "true", "t", "1" (case-insensitive T variants). Typical accepted false forms include: "false", "f", "0" (case-insensitive F variants). Arbitrary other strings may be rejected.
An unconstrained text string with no specific required format. May contain any bytes/characters; typically used for messages, help text, or names.

generators.generator:
import random
from typing import List

# Generator for boolean text tokens suitable for cxxopts::values::parser_tool::IsTrueText/IsFalseText
# The fuzz stubs call FUZZ_PARAM_STR() to obtain a std::string. We will return a bytes buffer
# that the harness will split into one or more strings. Since we only control one buffer,
# we pack a single token per buffer to maximize the chance it is used directly as the parameter.
# We bias generation toward canonical true/false representations and include varied casing,
# surrounding whitespace, and optional plus/minus signs that are still commonly considered valid
# or at least interesting but typically remain valid C strings.

TRUE_CANON = [
    "true", "t", "1", "TRUE", "True", "TrUe"
]
FALSE_CANON = [
    "false", "f", "0", "FALSE", "False", "FaLsE"
]

# Additional interesting, but valid textual forms that libraries sometimes accept
# Note: cxxopts documented set is limited; these variants help exercise negative paths too.
TRUE_VARIANTS = [
    "yes", "y", "+1", "on", "enable"
]
FALSE_VARIANTS = [
    "no", "n", "-0", "off", "disable"
]

WHITESPACE_PREFIX = ["", " ", "\t", "\n", "\r\n", "  \t"]
WHITESPACE_SUFFIX = ["", " ", "\t", "\n", "\r\n", "\t  "]

DECORATORS = [
    ("", ""),           # plain
    ("\"", "\""),     # quoted
    ("'", "'"),          # single quoted
]

NOISE = [
    "", "maybe", "2", "-1", "tru", " fals", "00", "10", "tRue!", "fAlse?",
    "null", "nil", "NaN", "[]", "{}", "--true", "--false"
]

def _pick_weighted(rng: random.Random, items: List[str], weights: List[int]) -> str:
    total = sum(weights)
    x = rng.randrange(total)
    cum = 0
    for item, w in zip(items, weights):
        cum += w
        if x < cum:
            return item
    return items[-1]

def _maybe_ws(rng: random.Random, s: str) -> str:
    pre = rng.choice(WHITESPACE_PREFIX)
    suf = rng.choice(WHITESPACE_SUFFIX)
    return f"{pre}{s}{suf}"

def _maybe_decorate(rng: random.Random, s: str) -> str:
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        l, r = rng.choice(DECORATORS)
        return f"{l}{s}{r}"
    return s

def _build_token(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Choose a family: true, false, variant true, variant false, or noise
    families = ["true", "false", "tvar", "fvar", "noise"]
    # Bias towards canonical accepted forms to ensure valid paths are hit often
    weights = [35, 35, 10, 10, 10]
    fam = _pick_weighted(rng, families, weights)

    if fam == "true":
        core = rng.choice(TRUE_CANON)
    elif fam == "false":
        core = rng.choice(FALSE_CANON)
    elif fam == "tvar":
        core = rng.choice(TRUE_VARIANTS)
    elif fam == "fvar":
        core = rng.choice(FALSE_VARIANTS)
    else:
        core = rng.choice(NOISE)

    token = _maybe_ws(rng, core)
    token = _maybe_decorate(rng, token)
    return token


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    token = _build_token(rng)
    # Ensure non-empty; if empty noise chosen plus empty whitespace/decorators, fallback to "true"
    if not token:
        token = "true"
    data = token.encode("utf-8", errors="strict")
    # Limit total size to 4096 bytes
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]
    return data

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator produces interesting arbitrary strings suitable for cxxopts fuzzing stubs.
# Focus: program names, help strings, and exception messages. We include a wide variety of
# lengths, unicode, whitespace patterns, punctuation, commas, dashes, and typical CLI tokens.

_MAX_BYTES = 4096

_ASCII_PRINTABLE = (
    string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + " "
)

# Diverse unicode samples including combining marks, RTL, emoji, CJK, and separators
_UNICODE_SAMPLES = [
    "こんにちは",            # Japanese
    "Привет",               # Russian
    "مرحبا",                # Arabic (RTL script)
    "שלום",                 # Hebrew (RTL)
    "नमस्ते",               # Devanagari
    "你好世界",               # Chinese
    "안녕하세요",              # Korean
    "😀😃😄😁😆",            # Emojis
    "Z̷a̷l̷g̷o̷",            # Combining marks
    "e\x1b[31mred\x1b[0m", # ANSI escapes as text
    "𝔘𝔫𝔦𝔠𝔬𝔡𝔢",             # Mathematical Fraktur
    "𝑈𝑛𝑖𝑐𝑜𝑑𝑒",             # Mathematical italic
    "\tTabbed\ttext",     # Tabs
    "Line1\nLine2\nLine3",
    "Name-With.Dots_and_Underscores",
    "option1,option2,option-three,option_four",  # cxxopts-style comma list
    "--long-option --another -abc -x=42",
]

# Reasonable program names typical for argv[0]
_PROG_NAMES = [
    "prog",
    "myapp",
    "tool",
    "cli",
    "cxxopts-demo",
    "parser",
    "opt",
    "util",
]

# Help/usage fragments
_HELP_FRAGMENTS = [
    "Usage: prog [OPTIONS] input...",
    "Options:\n  -h, --help    Show this help\n  -v, --version Print version",
    "Examples:\n  prog -o out --flag file1 file2",
    "This is a long help paragraph describing how to use the tool effectively.",
    "[OPTION...]",
    "positional parameters",
]

# Exception-like messages
_EXC_FRAGMENTS = [
    "Invalid option format 'abc'",
    "Option 'name' already exists",
    "Argument '-x' starts with a - but has incorrect syntax",
    "Option '--file' is missing an argument",
    "Option '--flag' does not take an argument, but argument 'yes' given",
    "Option '--value' requires an argument",
    "Option '--unknown' does not exist",
]

def _rand_bool(r: random.Random, p: float) -> bool:
    return r.random() < p

def _rand_ascii(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return "".join(r.choice(_ASCII_PRINTABLE) for _ in range(n))

def _rand_unicode(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    # Build by concatenating chosen unicode samples and some random ascii
    parts: List[str] = []
    target = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    while sum(len(p) for p in parts) < target:
        choice = r.choice(_UNICODE_SAMPLES)
        parts.append(choice)
        if _rand_bool(r, 0.4):
            parts.append(_rand_ascii(r, 0, 6))
    s = "".join(parts)
    # Trim to target length in characters
    if len(s) > target:
        s = s[:target]
    return s

def _make_program_name(r: random.Random) -> str:
    base = r.choice(_PROG_NAMES)
    # Occasionally append version/style suffixes, but keep <= 64 for stub
    if _rand_bool(r, 0.7):
        suffixes = ["", "-v1", "-dbg", ".exe", "-α", "_test", "-tool"]
        base += r.choice(suffixes)
    # Ensure non-empty and modest length
    return base[:64] if base else "prog"

def _make_help(r: random.Random) -> str:
    pieces = []
    # Compose from fragments and unicode; cap length to 128 for stubs
    for _ in range(r.randint(1, 4)):
        pieces.append(r.choice(_HELP_FRAGMENTS))
    if _rand_bool(r, 0.5):
        pieces.append(_rand_unicode(r, 5, 40))
    if _rand_bool(r, 0.5):
        pieces.append("\n")
        pieces.append(_rand_ascii(r, 0, 20))
    s = " \n".join(pieces)
    return s[:128]

def _make_exception_message(r: random.Random) -> str:
    if _rand_bool(r, 0.6):
        base = r.choice(_EXC_FRAGMENTS)
    else:
        base = _rand_ascii(r, 5, 60)
    if _rand_bool(r, 0.5):
        base += " | " + _rand_unicode(r, 0, 30)
    return base

def _pick_mode(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Modes correspond to different fuzz stubs using FUZZ_PARAM_STR
    return r.choice(["prog", "help", "exception", "generic"]) 

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    mode = _pick_mode(r)

    if mode == "prog":
        s = _make_program_name(r)
    elif mode == "help":
        s = _make_help(r)
    elif mode == "exception":
        s = _make_exception_message(r)
    else:
        # Generic arbitrary string: mix of ascii/unicode, include tokens relevant to cxxopts
        parts: List[str] = []
        for _ in range(r.randint(2, 6)):
            choice = r.randint(0, 4)
            if choice == 0:
                parts.append(_rand_ascii(r, 1, 30))
            elif choice == 1:
                parts.append(_rand_unicode(r, 1, 40))
            elif choice == 2:
                # Comma-separated option names to hit split_option_names
                names = []
                for _ in range(r.randint(1, 5)):
                    # Start with alnum, then allowed chars [-_.?]
                    head = r.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits)
                    tail_len = r.randint(0, 8)
                    tail_chars = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_._?"
                    tail = "".join(r.choice(tail_chars) for _ in range(tail_len))
                    names.append(head + tail)
                parts.append(",".join(names))
            elif choice == 3:
                # Long option with possible value
                name = "--" + _make_program_name(r).replace(" ", "-")
                if _rand_bool(r, 0.5):
                    val = str(r.randint(-1000, 1000))
                    parts.append(f"{name}={val}")
                else:
                    parts.append(name)
            else:
                # Short option grouping
                letters = ''.join(r.choice(string.ascii_letters) for _ in range(r.randint(1, 5)))
                seg = "-" + letters
                if _rand_bool(r, 0.3):
                    seg += "=" + str(r.randint(0, 255))
                parts.append(seg)
        s = " ".join(parts)

    b = s.encode("utf-8", errors="surrogatepass")
    if len(b) > _MAX_BYTES:
        b = b[:_MAX_BYTES]
    return b
